summary: The memory-saving scoring refactor appears logically sound: row-order keys are recreated consistently, merges are asserted, blank-name agreement is prevented, and the birth-date restriction is preserved. The main unresolved problem is replication: this analysis remains outside the replication master, while its only new launcher is machine-specific and cannot build the required input.

findings.title: The profile-name results still cannot be reproduced by the replication master
findings.what_the_code_does: The new launcher only executes `capture noisily do "D:\repos\fixing_transcription_errors\MATCHING\profile_names_score.do"` and prints `_rc`. The score script reads a pre-existing `profile_names.dta`, while its build script depends on the literal `E:/multigen_CM/DATA/INTERMEDIATE`. The replication master runs its fixed `local scripts` list and `foreach s in fs_avg_performance fs_cells`, neither of which includes the profile build or score step.
findings.why_it_matters: A standard replication run cannot create the input dataset or regenerate `MATCHING/results/profile_names.md`. The appendix result can therefore be absent or stale, and an external replicator cannot reproduce it without reconstructing undocumented machine-specific paths and manually choosing the execution order.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "profile_names_(build|score)|profile_names\.dta|profile_names\.md|multigen_CM" replication MATCHING/_run_profile_names_score.do MATCHING/profile_names_build.do MATCHING/profile_names_score.do` and confirm that the replication master contains no invocation or preflight for these files.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the profile scrape root to `replication/config.do`, document and preflight the required profile inputs, invoke `profile_names_build.do` followed by `profile_names_score.do` from the appropriate replication master, and have the driver track the generated Markdown output. If the standalone launcher is retained, derive its path from `$REP_REPO` and return a nonzero failure status rather than merely printing `_rc`.

verified_clean.item: The low-memory refactor preserves row alignment across the separately loaded name columns.
verified_clean.evidence: Each reference extract creates `_id = _n`, saves one row per original observation, and the main dataset recreates the same key before three `merge 1:1` operations with `assert(match)` at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:102-109 and MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:118-130.

verified_clean.item: Normalization collisions do not create a many-to-one merge error.
verified_clean.evidence: `xsplit` deduplicates the normalized source before `extrname`, then merges the resulting unique map back with `merge m:1`; `refsplit` subsequently retains one row per distinct original source value at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:69-87 and MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:94-105.

verified_clean.item: Empty source strings cannot inflate agreement rates.
verified_clean.evidence: Every first-name and surname match indicator explicitly requires the normalized transcription to be nonempty at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:160-165; score denominators also require the applicable reference component at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:201-215.

verified_clean.item: The birth-date robustness restriction is unchanged in substance by dropping the wide string column early.
verified_clean.evidence: The code constructs `has_birth = birthdate!=""` before dropping `birthdate`, then supplies `has_birth` as the extra score condition at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:125-127 and MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:250-251.

verified_clean.item: The generated output does not present profile agreement as accuracy and discloses the principal common-source concern.
verified_clean.evidence: The source comments call the measure selected-reference agreement and explain FamilySearch favoritism at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:25-31; the generated description repeats that this is not accuracy and identifies the FamilySearch-linked reference at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:176-178.

verified_clean.item: The scoring code exposes major sample restrictions rather than silently describing the result as population-wide.
verified_clean.evidence: The output description identifies the 49-state, human-complete, one-to-one-linked, gender-screened sample, and the following table reports stored selection counts at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:178-191.

verified_clean.item: Surname-only blocks no longer condition unnecessarily on a usable profile first name.
verified_clean.evidence: Only `kind=="full"` requires both `ref_first` and the surname reference; the surname-only branch requires only `ref_`r'!=""` at MATCHING/profile_names_score.do:207-215.

verified_clean.item: No stochastic operation in the changed scoring code requires a random seed.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_score.do consists of deterministic loads, normalization, deduplication, asserted merges, filtering, and aggregation; no sampling or random-number command appears.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims emitted by or documented within the changed code; paper prose and reported paper numbers could not be checked.
The external datasets were unavailable, so observation counts, normalized-name distributions, and realized agreement percentages could not be verified.
The Stata pipeline could not be executed in this environment. Runtime conclusions are based on source inspection, including Stata merge and macro semantics.
The review target was the uncommitted working tree; unchanged code outside the dependencies needed to interpret these changes was not comprehensively audited.
